p0.original: 关键问题：思维的组成成分是什么
p0.en: Questions: What is the composition of thinking?

p2.original: 思维是一种认知过程。在此过程中，大脑运用来自感觉、情绪和记忆的信息去创造并操控诸如概念、图像、图式和脚本等心理表征。
p2.en: Thinking is a cognitive process. In doing so, the brain uses information from feelings, emotions and memories to create and manipulate psychological manifestations such as concepts, images, patterns and scripts.

p3.original: 解决一个数学问题，决定周五晚上要做什么，以及沉浸在自己的白日梦中，这些都需要思维。我们可以将思维看作一种复杂的认知行为——大脑中的信息加工——我们通过它来处理我们的思想、图像、情感、欲望和经验所构成的世界。正如核心概念6.1所指出的，这种信息可以来自内部，也可以来自外部，但它总是涉及某种形式的心理表征。
p3.en: Addressing a mathematical problem, deciding what to do on Friday night and immersing in their daydreams requires thinking. We can see thinking as a complex cognitive behaviour — information processing in the brain — through which we deal with the world that our thoughts, images, emotions, desires and experiences make up. As noted in core concept 6.1, this information can come from either internal or external sources, but it always involves some form of psychological representation.

p4.original: 思维是一种认知过程。在此过程中，大脑运用来自感觉、情绪和记忆的信息去创造并操控诸如概念、图像、图式和脚本等心理表征。
p4.en: Thinking is a cognitive process. In doing so, the brain uses information from feelings, emotions and memories to create and manipulate psychological manifestations such as concepts, images, patterns and scripts.

p5.original: 这些心理表征便充当了认知的组成成分，而思维则以有意义的方式将它们组织起来。最终的结果就是一些更高级的思维过程，我们称之为推理、想象、判断、决策、问题解决、专业知识、创造力，以及天赋。
p5.en: These psychological manifestations serve as components of the perception, while thinking organizes them in a meaningful way. The end result is a more advanced process of thinking, which we call reasoning, imagination, judgement, decision-making, problem resolution, expertise, creativity and talent.

p7.en: 6.1 The psychological categories of the concept are explained.

p8.original: 6.2 解释为什么人们的认知地图可能有很大不同。
p8.en: 6.2 Explain why people's cognitive maps may vary considerably.

p9.original: 6.3 描述PET扫描、MRI与fMRI在揭示思维和大脑的作用中扮演了什么角色。
p9.en: 6.3 Describe the role of PET scans, MRI and fMRI in revealing the role of mind and brain.

p10.original: 6.4 将直觉视为思维的情绪性成分。
p10.en: 6.4 Intuitive perception as an emotional component of thinking.

p13.en: The psychological type of interpretation of the concept.

p14.original: 你是否曾有过去一个新地方，却感觉自己以前到过这里的经历？或者与某人交谈，然后感觉这段经历似曾相识？如果你有过这样的经历，就体验过一种被称作既视感（déjà vu，来自法语，意思是“以前见过”）的现象。这个术语指的是这样一种奇怪的感觉：觉得自己当前的经历是以前经历过的，尽管自己并不能提取出那段外显记忆。这种感觉反映了大脑具有将新刺激作为熟悉类别的样例来处理的能力，即使这个刺激与在此之前遇到的任何刺激都略有不同。为什么这很重要呢？例如，想象一下，如果每次在学校开始一堂新课，我们都无法想起任何先前的学校经历，因而我们必须从头开始弄清楚我们应该做什么、如何学习，甚至是学校的意义所在，那么生活将会是什么样子的。这种将经历、物体或观点同化为熟悉的心理类别——对它们采取相同措施或给它们贴上相同标签——的能力是能够思考的生物体最基本的属性之一（Mervis & Rosch，1981）。
p14.en: Have you ever had a new place in the past and you feel like you've been here before? Or talk to someone and feel like you've known each other? If you've had that experience, you've experienced a phenomenon called déjà vu, which is French, which means "had seen before." The term refers to the strange feeling that the current experience is one that has been experienced in the past, even though it does not extract the outward memory. This perception reflects the ability of the brain to treat new incentives as a sample of familiar categories, even though this stimulus is slightly different from any that it has previously encountered. Why is this important? Imagine, for example, what life would be like if, every time we start a new class at school, we could not recall any previous school experience, so we had to start from the beginning to figure out what we should do, how we should learn, and even what schools mean. This ability to assimilate experiences, objects or views into familiar psychological categories — adopting the same measures or labelling them — is one of the most basic attributes of living organisms that can be considered (Mervis & Rosch, 1981).

p15.original: 我们以这种方式所形成的心理类别被称为概念（concept）。我们将概念当作思维的组成成分，因为它们帮助我们对知识进行组织（Goldman-Rakic，1992）。概念可以表征：
p15.en: The psychological category that we have developed in this way is known as concept. We see concepts as components of our thinking because they help us organize knowledge (Goldman-Rakic, 1992). The concept can be expressed as follows:

p16.original: 物体的类别（class of objects），如“椅子”或“食物”；
p16.en: Type of object (class of objects), e.g. “chair” or “food”;

p17.original: 生物体（living organism），如“鸟”或“水牛”；

p19.en: Properties (property), such as " red " or " large ";

p22.en: Processes, such as how to tie shoes;

p23.original: 意图（intention），如打断谈话的意图（Smith & Medin，1981）。
p23.en: Intent, such as the intention to interrupt the conversation (Smith & Medin, 1981).

p24.original: 但由于概念是心理结构，因此我们不能直接观察它们。对认知科学家而言，这意味着要从概念对行为或脑活动的影响中来推断概念。例如，你无法确定另一个人对“有趣”这个概念的定义是否和你的一样，但是你可以观察这个人对你认为“有趣”的刺激做出的反应是否和你的反应一样，来做出判断。
p24.en: But because the concepts are psychological structures, we cannot observe them directly. For cognitive scientists, this means deduced from the impact of the concept on behaviour or brain activity. For example, you cannot be sure that another person defines the concept of “interesting”, as you do, but you can see whether this person's response to the stimulus you think is “interesting” is the same as your response.

p26.original: 每个人都在运用独特的方式对世界进行概念化，所以我们的概念定义了我们是谁。但是，在这种个体独特性的背后，也存在着所有人形成概念的方式的相似性。尤为特别的是，我们都对自然概念（natural concept）和人工概念（artificial concept）进行了区分（Medin et al.，2000）。
p26.en: Everyone is using a unique way to conceptualize the world, so our concept defines who we are. However, behind this uniqueness of the individual there is also a similarity in the way in which everyone forms the concept. In particular, we all distinguish between the concept of nature (natural concept) and the concept of artificial concept (Medin et al., 2000).

p27.original: 你对“鸟”的自然概念所涉及的原型可能更像鹰而非企鹅。因此，你把老鹰识别为鸟的速度可能会比识别企鹅更快。然而，动物学专业的学生，可能也有一个“鸟”的人工概念，其对老鹰和企鹅同等适用。
p27.en: Your natural concept of birds may involve prototypes more like eagles than penguins. So, you're probably going to recognize the eagle as a bird faster than you are. However, students in Zoology may also have an artificial concept of “birds”, which applies equally to eagles and penguins.

p28.original: 1. 自然概念是不精确的心理类别，是从我们有关这个世界的日常经验中发展出来的。基于你与鸟的经验，你拥有了关于“鸟”的自然概念。这反过来又形成了一个心理原型（prototype），一个来自你的经验的代表典型鸟类的一般图像（Hunt，1989）。要判断一个物体是不是鸟，你会在头脑中将它与你的鸟的原型进行对比——它与原型越匹配，你就能越快地做出判断。例如，大多数人将鹰识别为鸟的速度要快于将企鹅识别为鸟的速度（Rips，1997）。我们的个人原型包含了各种各样的自然概念，包括友谊、亲密感和性，而且对于所有这些自然概念，一个人的原型可能不同于其他人的，这就为我们关系中误解的产生创造了基础。由于自然概念的不精确性，它们有时被称为“模糊概念”（Kosko & Isaka，1993）。
p28.en: 1. The concept of nature is an imprecise psychological category that has evolved from our daily experience of the world. Based on your experience with birds, you have a natural concept of birds. This, in turn, has created a psychological prototype (prototype), a generic image of typical birds from your experience (Hunt, 1989). To judge whether an object is a bird, you compare it in your head with the prototype -- the more it matches the prototype, the faster you can judge. For example, most people identify eagles as birds faster than they identify penguins as birds (Rips 1997). Our personal prototype encompasses a wide variety of natural concepts, including friendship, intimacy and sexuality, and for all these natural concepts, the prototype of one person may be different from others, which creates the basis for the creation of misunderstandings in our relations. Because of the inaccuracy of natural concepts, they are sometimes referred to as “obsolute concepts” (Kosko & Isaka, 1993).

p29.original: 2. 相比之下，人工概念由一组规则或特征定义，如字典定义或数学公式。对“矩形”的定义就是一个例子。人工概念代表了被精确定义的观点或抽象概念，而非实际物体。所以，如果你学的是动物学专业，那么你可能也有一个关于“鸟”的人工概念，将鸟定义为一种“有羽毛的两足动物”。事实上，你在学校里学习的大部分概念都是人工概念。例如，“认知心理学”，甚至是“概念”本身！
p29.en: 2. By contrast, the concept of artificiality is defined by a set of rules or features, such as dictionary definitions or mathematical formulae. The definition of “retrogressive” is an example. Artificial concepts represent precisely defined views or abstract concepts rather than actual objects. So, if you're studying Zoology, you may also have an artificial concept of "birds", which defines birds as a "two-legged animal with feathers." In fact, most of the concepts you learn in school are artificial. For example, “cognitive psychology”, even “concepts” themselves!

p31.original: 我们将我们大部分的陈述性记忆组织为概念层级（concept hierarchy），它按照从一般到具体的层级进行排列，如图6-1所示。对大多数人来说，“动物”的广义概念有几个子类别。例如，“鸟”和“鱼”，这些子类别又相应地被分为几个具体的形式——“金丝雀”“鸵鸟”“鲨鱼”和“鲑鱼”。“动物”这个类别本身可能就是“生物”这个更大类别的一个子类别。此外，我们常常会把每个类别与各种其他概念联系在一起。例如，有些鸟是可以被食用的，有一些是濒危的，还有一些则被作为国家的象征。由此一来，我们的概念层级就是概念及与其相关联的错综复杂的网络。
p31.en: We have organized most of our narrative memory as a conceptual hierarchy (concept hierarchy), organized by a hierarchy from general to specific levels, as shown in figure 6-1. For most people, the broad concept of “animal” has several subcategories. For example, “birds” and “fish”, which in turn are divided into several specific forms — “creams” — “octopus” “sharks” and “salmons”. The category of “animal” may itself be a subcategory of the larger category of “living”. In addition, we often link each category to various other concepts. For example, some birds can be eaten, some are endangered and others are used as symbols of the State. Thus, our conceptual hierarchy is the concept and the complex networks associated with it.

p32.original: 图6-1 概念的层级组织结构
p32.en: Figure 6-1: The hierarchical organizational structure of the concept

p35.original: 在看过图6-1之后，选择一个你自己的广义概念，如学校、运动、娱乐、环境、艺术等。然后为你所选的概念确定3个子类别（层级2）及每个子类别的两个种类（层级3）。
p35.en: After looking at figure 6-1, choose a broad concept of your own, such as school, sports, recreation, environment, art, etc. The concept selected for you is then defined as three subcategories (level 2) and two categories (level 3) for each subcategory.

p37.original: 同一概念在不同文化中蕴含的意义大不相同。
p37.en: The meaning of the same concept varies greatly across cultures.

p38.original: 一方面，在处理冲突观点和矛盾的方式上，西方人与许多东方人不同（Peng & Nisbett，1999）。
p38.en: On the one hand, Westerners are different from many Easterners in the way they deal with conflicting views and contradictions (Peng & Nisbett, 1999).

p39.original: 另一方面，还有一个很大的文化差异涉及对逻辑的运用。许多文化并不像西方文化那样重视逻辑推理的运用（Bower，2000a；Nisbett et al.，2001）。一些文化会通过将新观点与一些宗教著作中的智慧进行比较来寻求“真理”。即使在美国，许多人也更看重所谓的“常识”。它指的是基于经验而非逻辑的思考。
p39.en: On the other hand, there is a significant cultural difference that relates to the application of logic. Many cultures do not attach the same importance to the application of logic as Western cultures (Bower, 2000a); Nisbett et al., 2001). Some cultures seek “truth” by comparing new ideas with wisdom in some religious writings. Even in the United States, so-called “common sense” is more important to many. It means thinking based on experience, not logic.

p40.original: 我们从这些文化差异中可以学到什么呢？虽然存在一些跨文化的普遍的思维原则，但它们涉及的只是十分基本的过程。例如，每个人都会形成概念这样的事实。然而，对于人们如何形成概念或概念被赋予什么含义，对假定别人想的和我们一样这件事，我们应更加慎重。
p40.en: What can we learn from these cultural differences? While there are some universal principles of intercultural thinking, they involve only very basic processes. For example, the fact that everyone has a concept is a fact. However, we should be more cautious about how people shape concepts or what they give meaning to them, about what others assume to be like us.

p43.original: 解释为什么人们的认知地图可能有很大不同。
p43.en: Explain why people's cognitive maps may be quite different.

p44.original: 我们用语言进行思考，但也会用图片、空间关系以及其他感觉图像进行思考。如果你花点时间想一想一个朋友的脸、你最喜欢的歌或热曲奇的气味，你就能轻而易举地感受到这一点。视觉表象为我们的思维增添了复杂性和丰富性，涉及其他感觉（听、味、嗅、触）的表象亦是如此。对于有些问题，用图像比用语言能更清楚地厘清关系，解决这类问题时，使用感觉表象进行思考将非常有帮助。这就是为什么像本书这样的图书作品常常要用图片、图解和图表来鼓励人们运用视觉思维。
p44.en: We think in language, but also in pictures, in space, and other sensory images. If you think about a friend's face, your favorite song, or the smell of hot cookies, you can easily feel it. Visual appearances add complexity and richness to our thinking, as do those involving other feelings (hearing, smell, smelling). In some cases, the relationship is more clearly clarified by image than by language, and it would be very helpful to think through the use of sensory appearances in solving such problems. That's why books like this often use pictures, illustrations and graphs to encourage people to use visual thinking.

p45.original: 视觉概念的一种特殊形式是对物理空间的认知表征，其被称作认知地图。认知地图可以帮助你去你的心理学教室，还能让你指引朋友去附近的剧院或熟食店。通过使用认知地图，人们可以闭着眼睛在自己家中穿梭或去熟悉的目的地，甚至在他们的惯常路线被阻断时也能做到。
p45.en: A special form of the visual concept is the cognitive expression of the physical space, known as the cognitive map. Cognitive maps can help you to go to your psychology class, and you can guide your friends to a nearby theater or deli. Through the use of cognitive maps, people can travel their homes behind closed eyes or to familiar destinations, even when their usual routes are blocked.

p46.original: 不过，不同的人的认知地图可能会有很大不同。就像思维的其他元素一样，认知地图建立在我们独特的知觉基础上。我们的心理地图反映了我们从自身文化视角发展出来的世界观。
p46.en: However, the cognitive maps of different people may vary considerably. Like other elements of thinking, cognitive maps are based on our unique consciousness. Our psychological map reflects the world view that we have developed from our own cultural perspective.

p47.original: 我们都会使用认知地图为自己探索世界提供导航。你是不是好奇，想看看自己的认知地图工作得怎样？
p47.en: We all use cognitive maps to provide navigation for our exploration of the world. Are you curious to see how your cognitive map works?

p50.original: 描述PET扫描、MRI与fMRI在揭示思维和大脑的作用中扮演了什么角色。
p50.en: Describe the role of PET scans, MRI and fMRI in revealing the role of thinking and the brain.

p51.original: 脑成像的发展使认知研究人员能够开始绘制思维自身的图谱（Ashby & Waldron，2000）。科学家现在能够将大脑中想的事物，如“狗”或“铅笔”，与特定的脑电波模式对应起来（Garnsey，1993；Osterhout & Holcomb，1992）。他们给志愿者的头“连”上电极以记录其脑电反应，然后给其反复呈现一个刺激（如在屏幕上闪现“狗”这个单词），以此来找到二者的对应。虽然仅一个试次的脑电波可能无法显示出清晰的模式，但计算机可以对单一、重复刺激（如一个声音信号或视觉图像）的许多脑电波反应进行处理，消除大脑的随机背景中的“噪声”，并分离出由某个刺激引发的独特的脑电波模式（Kotchoubey，2002）。
p51.en: The development of brain imaging has enabled cognitive researchers to begin drawing their own picture of thinking (Ashby & Waldron, 2000). Scientists are now able to match what they think in the brain, such as a “dog” or a “crunch”, to a specific brain wave pattern (Garnesey, 1993); Osterhout & Holcomb, 1992. They put the brain electrodes on the heads of volunteers to record their brain electrodes, and then re-emerge them with an irritation (e.g. flashing the word “dog” on the screen) to find a match between them. While a single test brain wave may not show a clear pattern, computers can treat many brain waves that are a single, repeated irritation (e.g., a sound signal or visual image), eliminate “noise” in the random background of the brain and isolate unique brain waves that are triggered by a single irritation (Kotchoube, 2002).

p52.original: 其他研究方法则可以告诉我们，当我们进行思考时，大脑的哪些部分被激活，哪些部分被抑制。通过使用PET扫描、MRI和fMRI，神经科学家们已经确定了在各种心理任务中会变得活跃的大脑区域。这类工作得出了两项主要结论。
p52.en: Other research methods can tell us which parts of the brain are activated and which parts are suppressed when we think about it. Through the use of PET scans, MRI and fMRI, neuroscientists have identified brain regions that can become active in various psychological missions. Two main conclusions emerged from such work.

p53.original: 1. 思考是一种涉及大脑中广泛分布的各个区域的共同活动，而不是仅取决于一个“思维中心”。
p53.en: Thinking is a common activity involving a wide range of regions in the brain, rather than relying solely on a “centre of thought”.

p54.original: 2. 神经科学家现在将大脑看作一个由各种高度专业化模块所组成的共同体，其中各个模块会处理思维的不同成分（Cree & McRae，2003）。
p54.en: 2. Neuroscientists now see the brain as a community of highly specialized modules that deal with different components of thinking (Cree & McRae, 2003).

p55.original: 此外，大脑生成图像的思维回路与它在感觉和知觉图像时使用的回路是一样的。因此，从记忆中提取的视觉表象激活了视觉皮层，而听觉记忆则激活了听觉皮层（Behrmann，2000）。用语言进行思考则可能会根据话题的不同而涉及不同的区域。一项脑成像研究表明，大多数笑话主要通过皮层中的语言加工区域让我们感到开心，而“谐音梗”则激活大脑中的声音加工回路（Goel & Dolan，2001）。总体来说，这项工作显示，思考是一个由许多模块协同运作的过程。
p55.en: In addition, the brain produces images with the same thought loop as it uses when it feels and perceives images. Thus, visual appearances extracted from memory activate the visual cortex, while hearing memory activates the hearing cortex (Behrmann, 2000). Rethinking in language may involve different regions depending on the subject matter. A study of brain imaging shows that most jokes make us happy mainly through language processing areas in the cortex, while the “harmonic infarction” activates voice processing circuits in the brain (Goel & Dolan, 2001). In general, this exercise shows that thinking is a process that is coordinated by many modules.

p56.original: 大脑额叶（frontal lobe）在协调我们决策和解决问题时的心理活动方面发挥着尤为重要的作用（Helmuth，2003a；Koechlin et al.，2003）。为了做到这一点，前额皮层（位于额叶，就在你眼睛的上方）要执行三项不同的任务：
p56.en: The frontal lobe plays a particularly important role in coordinating our psychological activities in decision-making and problem-solving (Helmuth, 2003a); Koechlin et al., 2003. In order to do this, the front cortex (at the top of your eye, on the forehead) has three different tasks to perform:

p57.original: 1. 跟踪情境（episode，我们所处的情境）；
p57.en: 1. Following the situation (episode, where we are);

p59.original: 3. 对情境中的特定刺激（stimulus）做出反应。
p59.en: 3. Respond to specific stimulus in the situation.

p60.original: 以下是它的工作原理。假定你正开车去学校，你看到路边有一只受伤的狗（情境），它显然还活着，但是似乎无法行走（刺激）。你会怎么做？如果这是在你家附近，并且你认出了这只狗，你很有可能会停下来予以帮助，你也许会帮忙找到狗的主人或带它去看兽医。但是如果你不住在附近，而且你也不认识这只狗呢？或者如果你正赶赴一场考试，而停下来帮忙可能会导致你迟到，甚至错过考试呢？如果你害怕狗呢？这些不同的背景会影响你的决定，而所有这些仅在几秒内就能完成。从神经科学的角度来看，有趣的是所有这些任务都是由大脑模块以不同组合的形式、以无缝同步的方式来共同完成的。这是一个令人印象深刻的复杂系统。
p60.en: Here's how it works. Assuming you were driving to school, you saw an injured dog on the side of the road, apparently alive, but apparently unable to walk (stimulate). What would you do? If this is near your house, and you recognize the dog, you'll probably stop to help, and you might help find the dog's owner or take it to the vet. But what if you don't live around and you don't know the dog? Or if you're on your way to an exam and you stop to help, it might cause you to be late or even miss the exam? What if you're afraid of dogs? These different backgrounds will influence your decisions, and all of them can be done in just a few seconds. From a neuroscientific point of view, it is interesting that all of these tasks are carried out jointly by brain modules in different combinations and in a seamlessly synchronized manner. It is an impressive and complex system.

p61.original: 这个fMRI扫描图显示的是那些处于热恋中的人们的大脑活动。边缘系统中与奖赏系统相关联的区域高度活跃，这与大脑对可卡因的反应相似。与思考、推理和计划有关的前额皮层也很活跃。
p61.en: This fMRI scan shows the brain activity of people who are in love. The regions associated with reward systems in peripheral systems are highly active, similar to brain reactions to cocaine. The frontal cortex associated with thought, reasoning and planning is also active.

p64.original: 将直觉视为思维的情绪性成分。
p64.en: Intuitives are seen as an emotional component of thinking.

p65.original: 心理学家早就知道，人们做决策时——甚至是进行重要决策（如买房或选择配偶）时——既会根据感受，又会根据理性做出快速判断（Gladwell，2005；Myers，2002）。当我们思考我们所处世界中的物体和事件时，我们会以被称为情绪的积极感受或消极感受来赋予它们“价值”。相应地，当我们从备选行动方案中做决策时，我们会根据赋予每种选择的情绪来给它们权重。当然，我们有能力更有条理和更有逻辑地去权衡这些选项，但情绪总是混入我们的决策中，特别是混入我们称为直觉（intuition）的快速思考过程中。
p65.en: Psychologists have long known that when people make decisions — even when they make important decisions (e.g. buying a house or choosing a spouse) — they can be judged on the basis of both feeling and reason (Gladwell, 2005); Myers, 2002. As we reflect on objects and events in the world in which we live, we give them “value” with what is called a positive or negative feeling of emotion. Accordingly, when we take decisions from alternative programmes of action, we give them weight in the light of the emotions that give each option. Of course, we have the capacity to weigh these options more coherently and logically, but emotions are always mixed in our decision-making, especially in the fast-thinking process that we call intuitive.

p66.original: 思维的这种情绪性成分——与许多其他复杂认知任务一样——会用到前额皮层。前额皮层让我们在做决策时无意识地考虑情绪性“预感”这个因素，包括让我们考虑关于过去经验的信息，以及我们的需求、欲望和情绪。前额皮层严重受损的个体可能无法表现情绪或存在直觉缺陷。因此，在面临决策时，他们常常会做出不明智的选择（Damasio，1994）。
p66.en: This emotional component of thinking — like many other complex cognitive tasks — can be used in the frontal cortex. The frontal cortex allows us to consciously consider the emotional “presension” factor in our decision-making, including information about past experiences, as well as our needs, desires and emotions. Individuals who have suffered severe pre-frontal cortex damage may not be able to express emotions or suffer from intuitive defects. As a result, they often make unwise choices when faced with decision-making (Damasio, 1994).

p67.original: 我们的直觉有多准确？你怎么看？
p67.en: How accurate are our instincts? What do you think?

p68.original: 有时，我们直觉性的快速判断仅仅是我们的偏见和偏向，虽然它们可能看似正确（Myers，2002）。在管理者身上这一点已被证实：他们常常高估自己的直觉的力量，相信自己特别善于判断别人的能力和性格。因此，即使研究表明将教育水平和测验分数等客观数据纳入考虑通常能帮助人们做出更好的判断，但管理者在招聘员工时还是常常仅依赖于面试（Dawes，2001）。
p68.en: Sometimes our intuitive quick judgement is just our prejudice and bias, although they may seem right (Myers, 2002). This has been confirmed in the case of managers: they often overestimate the power of their instincts and believe that they are particularly good at judging the abilities and character of others. Thus, even if studies have shown that taking objective data such as educational levels and test scores into account usually helps people make better judgements, managers often rely only on interviews when recruiting staff (Dawes, 2001).

p69.original: 然而，快速的直觉性判断有时会出乎意料地准确。纳里尼·安巴迪（Nalini Ambady）博士发现，人们在看过一个时长仅为6秒的视频片段后就能对一个人的人格特质做出极为准确的判断。同样，学生对一位教授的教学效果的快速判断与课程结束时的成绩高度相关（Ambady & Rosenthal，1993；Greer，2005）。普林斯顿大学（Princeton University）的心理学家丹尼尔·卡尼曼（Daniel Kahneman）认为，直觉是进化的产物，它帮助我们的祖先在困难和危险的情境中做出快速判断（Kahneman，2003）。
p69.en: However, rapid intuitive judgement can sometimes be unexpectedly accurate. Dr. Nalini Ambady found that a video clip of only six seconds' duration would make a very accurate judgement of a person's personality. Similarly, the quick judgement of a professor's educational effectiveness is highly relevant to the end of the course (Ambady & Rosenthal, 1993); Greer, 2005. Daniel Kahneman, a psychologist at Princeton University, believes that intuition is the product of evolution, which helps our ancestors to make quick judgements in difficult and dangerous circumstances (Kahneman, 2003).

p70.original: 6.4.1 什么时候可以依靠直觉
p70.en: 6.4.1 When can you rely on intuition?

p71.original: 那么，直觉的这些看似矛盾的发现让我们何去何从呢？直觉的准确性可能在某一方面依赖于我们使用它的背景。一般来说，我们对人格的“本能判断”通常都是准确的，但心理学家弗兰克·贝尔涅里（Frank Bernieri）指出一个案例，连环杀手泰德·邦迪（Ted Bundy）曾给人留下了很好的第一印象，这表明我们偶尔也会犯错（Winerman，2005c）。卡尼曼则表示，对于统计或数值判断，我们的直觉更有可能出错。（有多少英文单词以r结尾？我会被恐怖分子杀死的概率有多大？）我们将在接下来的内容中探讨这些特定错误的原因。
p71.en: So, where do these seemingly contradictory discoveries lead us to? Intuitive accuracy may depend in one way or another on the context in which we use it. In general, our “intuitive judgment” of personality is usually accurate, but the psychologist Frank Bernieri points to a case in which Ted Bundy, a serial killer, had a very good first impression, suggesting that we occasionally make mistakes (Winerman, 2005c). For its part, Kaniman indicated that our instincts were more likely to go wrong in terms of statistics or numerical judgements. (How many English words end in r? What are the chances that I will be killed by terrorists? We will look at the reasons for these particular errors in the next section.

p72.original: 除了背景因素，我们的直觉在时间受限的复杂情境中也可能更为可靠：在这些情境中，由于我们的工作记忆有限，依赖工作记忆的意识加工技能可能根本无法应对这种复杂性或大量的需要快速权衡的因素。举一个例子：某实验要求被试阅读一份介绍4间公寓的资料，其中每间公寓都有12个方面的介绍，他们需要从中选一间最佳公寓。这些介绍繁多且复杂，同时包括优点（“它所在的地区很好”）和缺点（“房东令人讨厌”）。该实验有3种实验条件：
p72.en: In addition to contextual factors, our intuition may also be more reliable in complex time-limited situations where, because of our limited work memory, the cognitive processing skills that depend on work memory may simply fail to cope with such complexity or a large number of factors that need to be weighed quickly. One example is an experiment that requires a trial reading of a document describing four apartments, each of which contains a description of 12 aspects from which they need to select the best apartment. These presentations are numerous and complex, and include both advantages (“it is well located in a good area”) and disadvantages (“landlords are annoying”). There are three experimental conditions for the experiment:

p73.original: 1. 一些被试必须立即进行选择；
p73.en: 1. Some of the tested must be selected immediately;

p74.original: 2. 一些被试有几分钟的仔细思考时间，然后再做选择；
p74.en: 2. Some have been tried for a few minutes to think carefully before making a choice;

p75.original: 3. 一些被试在阅读资料后，被一项乏味的任务分散了几分钟的注意力，然后才做选择。
p75.en: 3. Some of the people who were tried to read the material were distracted by a boring task for a few minutes before choosing.

p76.original: 在这些条件中，哪个条件测的是纯直觉？哪一组被试选择了最好的公寓？你怎么看？
p76.en: Which of these conditions is pure intuition? Which group was tested for the best apartment? What do you think?

p77.original: 第三个条件测的是纯直觉，因为虽然被试在接收信息与做出决定之间有几分钟时间，但是由于注意力被分散，他们没有机会进行认知分析。因此，他们必须凭直觉做出决定。实验结果令人振奋。注意分散（直觉）组的被试选出的最想要的公寓远好于其他组（Dijksterhuis，2004）。因此，在涉及时间有限或注意分散的复杂情境中，我们的直觉可能要比不完备的逻辑分析更具有指导意义。
p77.en: The third condition was pure intuition, since although they were tried for a few minutes between receiving the information and making the decision, they were not given the opportunity to undertake cognitive analysis because of the distraction. They must therefore take their decisions intuitively. The results of the experiment are encouraging. The most wanted apartments that have been tested for separation (intuitive) are much better than the others (Dijksterhuis, 2004). Therefore, in complex situations involving limited time or attention to fragmentation, our intuition may be more instructive than incomplete logical analysis.

p78.original: 然而，当选择与判断的时间较长时，专业知识就会发挥作用。一项研究（Pretz，2008）的结果表明了这一点，该研究比较了有经验的大学生与新手如何处理学校中的常见问题。对于耶鲁大学（Yale University）毕业班的学生来说，相较于简单跟随直觉，仔细思考能更有效地解决问题。相反，大一新生跟随直觉则会更成功。研究人员推测，当一个人拥有分析情境所需的专业知识时，直觉可能不利于其清晰地思考；而当一个人缺乏经验时，直觉胜过笨拙的分析。
p78.en: However, when selection and judgement take longer, expertise plays a role. This was demonstrated by the results of a study (Pretz, 2008) which compared the way experienced university students and beginners deal with common problems in schools. For the students of the Yale University graduation class, it is easier to think more carefully than simply following the instincts to solve problems more effectively. On the contrary, freshman freshman students follow the instincts more successfully. Researchers speculate that when a person has the expertise needed to analyse the situation, the intuition may be detrimental to his or her thinking in a clear manner; And when a person lacks experience, instincts are better than awkward analysis.

p79.original: 总而言之，重要的是认识到我们何时在进行直觉性判断，并思考当下的背景、可用时间，以及我们拥有的那个领域的专业知识。我们还须注意，直觉有可能不对，就像我们在讨论记忆时所看到的那样，信心并不是正确率的可靠指标。对心理学家而言，首要任务可能是帮助人们学会更精确地使用直觉（Haslam，2007）。就像一位研究人员所建议的那样，在许多情境中，对事实进行评估可能是最好的解决方案，之后再把处理权交给我们的无意识。通过这种方式，我们可能会学会在分析和直觉之间取得平衡（Dijksterhuis，2004）。
p79.en: In sum, it is important to recognize when we are making intuitive judgements and to reflect on the current context, the time available and the expertise we have in that field. We must also note that instincts may not be right, as we see when discussing memories, that confidence is not a reliable indicator of the correct rate. For psychologists, the first task may be to help people learn to use intuition more accurately (Haslam, 2007). As one researcher suggested, in many situations, assessment of the facts may be the best solution, and then we leave the handling to us unconsciously. In this way, we may learn to balance analysis and intuition (Dijksterhuis, 2004).

p80.original: 心理学很有用 图式与脚本帮助你知道要预期什么
p80.en: Psychology is useful. Graphics and scripts help you know what to expect.

p81.original: 你的很多知识都是以图式的形式存储在你的大脑中的（Oden，1987）。图式是为个体思考物体、事件、观点或者情绪提供框架的相关概念的集群。因而你可能有表征“学校”“互联网”“假期”“音乐”和“恐惧”的不同图式。让我们来看看运用这些图式的一些重要方式。
p81.en: A lot of your knowledge is stored in your brain in graphic form (Oden, 1987). The diagram is a cluster of concepts that provide a framework for individual thinking on objects, events, perspectives or emotions. So you may have a different pattern of “school” “Internet” “leave” “music” and “fear”. Let's look at some of the important ways in which these patterns are applied.

p83.original: 谷歌及其他搜索引擎所缺少的属性之一就是图式，因此，这些搜索引擎难以真正理解“生日”“心理学”或“脱脂摩卡”。然而对我们来说，当遇到熟悉的人、情境、图像及观点时，我们的有关图式为我们有可能发现它们有哪些特征这件事提供了背景和预期（Baldwin，1992）。例如，对于一位航空旅客来说，terminal（航站楼）这个词可能使他联想到包含人群、长走廊和飞机等场景的图式。然而，对于一位患有心脏病的人来说，他对terminal（患绝症的）的图式可能包含焦虑感和对死亡的思考。而对于一位汽车修理工而言，terminal（端子）则可能指的是一个电池电缆的接头。在所有这些例子中，我们的不同图式为同一个词的解释提供了不同的背景。
p83.en: One of the attributes missing from Google and other search engines is the pattern, which makes it difficult for those search engines to really understand “birthday” “psychology” or “defamation mocha”. For us, however, when we meet familiar people, circumstances, images and perspectives, our relevant graphics provide us with the background and expectations of what it is possible to find out about them (Baldwin, 1992). For example, for an air passenger, the term term term term term " terminal " may lead him to think of patterns that include crowds, long corridors and aircraft. However, for a person with a heart condition, his pattern of terminal (the terminally ill) may contain anxiety and reflection on death. For a car repairer, the terminal (end) may refer to the connection of a battery cable. In all these examples, our different patterns provide different contexts for the interpretation of the same term.

p84.original: 图式有助于我们快速做出决策，但图式驱动的决策并非总是明智的。芝加哥大学（The University of Chicago）的一名研究人员用电子游戏测试了人们的图式和预期对他们决策的影响。在游戏中，被试有不到1秒的时间判断图中人物携带的是手枪、钱包还是手机，之后他们必须选择按下射击或不射击的按钮。图式如何影响被试的判断？约书亚·科雷尔和他的同事们（Correll et al.，2007）发现被试的失误遵循了一个清晰的模式：手无寸铁的黑人比手无寸铁的白人更有可能被射击。这证明了图式与预期在我们思维过程中的力量。后续的研究表明，警察比平民更少犯错；而且对于所有被试来说，对游戏进行练习会提高正确率，这表明图式可以通过有意识的努力而被修正。
p84.en: Graphics help us to make decisions quickly, but they are not always wise. A researcher at the University of Chicago tested people's patterns and expected impacts on their decision-making using video games. In the game, the person on the map is tried for less than one second to carry a pistol, a wallet or a mobile phone, after which they must choose to press the button to shoot or not to shoot. How does the pattern influence the trial judgement? Joshua Corell and his colleagues (Correll et al., 2007) found that the error of the trial followed a clear pattern: unarmed blacks were more likely to be shot than unarmed whites. This proves the strength of the pattern and expectations in our thinking. Follow-up studies show that police officers make fewer mistakes than civilians; And for all the tests, practice on the game increases the correct rate, which suggests that the pattern can be modified by conscious effort.

p86.original: 这是科雷尔在研究图式如何影响我们做决策时所使用的图片例子。研究结果有力地证明了无意识图式如何造成了偏见和歧视。
p86.en: This is the example of a picture that Corlell used to study how the graphics affect our decision-making. The results of the study provide strong evidence of how the unconscious pattern leads to prejudice and discrimination.

p87.original: 新信息常常是不完整的或模棱两可的。当你能够将新信息与自己的图式中已有的知识相联系时，新信息才会变得更有意义。因此，图式可以帮助你推断出缺失的信息。思考下列语句：
p87.en: New information is often incomplete or ambiguous. New information becomes even more meaningful when you can link new information to the knowledge already available in your own chart. So, the pattern helps you to deduce the missing information. Think about the following statement:

p88.original: 打开篮子的那一刻，坦尼娅沮丧地发现，她忘了带盐。
p88.en: The moment Tanya opened the basket, it was frustrating to find that she forgot to bring salt.

p89.original: 在没有更多信息的情况下，你对上述情境会做出怎样的推断？盐这个词暗示了这个篮子是一个装有食物的野餐篮。坦尼娅对没有带盐感到沮丧这个事实表明，篮子中的食物通常是需要放盐的食物，如煮熟的鸡蛋。你会自然地判断出篮子里可能还会有什么食物，与此同时，哪些东西绝对不会出现在篮子里：世界上任何比野餐篮大的以及任何不适合带去野餐的东西——从巨蟒到镀铜的婴儿鞋。这样，你现在拥有的主要信息就都是围绕着“野餐篮”这个图式而组织的。因此，通过将有关坦尼娅的陈述与你的图式相关联，这个陈述便拥有了意义。
p89.en: How do you infer this situation in the absence of more information? The word salt suggests that the basket is a picnic basket with food. The fact that Tanya was frustrated with the lack of salt suggests that food in the basket is usually salted food, such as cooked eggs. You will naturally judge what else might be in the basket, and at the same time what will never appear in the basket: anything in the world bigger than a picnic basket and not fit to take a picnic — from an avid to a copper-plated baby shoe. So, the main message you have now is organized around the "cunt basket." Thus, by linking the statement about Tanya to your chart, it has meaning.

p90.original: 下面是图式理论的一个实际应用的例子。研究人员训练数学成绩偏低的学生将数学应用题分为几种不同的类型。例如，一种类型包含一个“变化”图式。学生们学习到，所有的“变化”问题都涉及一个故事，如“鲁迪（Rudy）有3便士，他的妈妈又给了他4便士，他现在有多少便士”。他们还学习了解决“变化”问题的常见策略。在几个月的基于图式的训练后，测验结果表明，这些学生的数学成绩提高得很快——足以进入“高于平均水平”的排名（Jitendra et al.，2007）。按图式对问题进行分类，帮助他们获得了解决问题的有效策略。
p90.en: The following is an example of a practical application of the graphical theory. Researchers train students who have low performance in mathematics to divide the subject of mathematical applications into several different types. For example, a type contains a “change” pattern. The students learned that all the “change” issues involved a story such as “Rudi has 3 pence, his mother gave him 4 pence, how many pence he has now”. They have also learned common strategies to address the issue of change. After several months of graphic-based training, the results of the tests showed that the students' mathematics performance had improved rapidly - enough to rank “higher than average” (Jitendra et al., 2007). The classification of issues by graphics has helped them to acquire effective strategies for solving problems.

p92.original: 日常生活中的许多幽默都以图式为基础（Dingfelder，2006）。当事情同时唤醒两个或更多不一致或不相容的图式时，我们常会觉得它很有趣。请思考这个笑话：
p92.en: Many of the humors in everyday life are based on graphics (Dingfelder, 2006). When things at the same time awaken two or more inconsistent or incompatible patterns, we often find them interesting. Please think about this joke:

p93.original: 一匹马走进一家酒吧，调酒师说：“为什么你拉着一张长脸？”
p93.en: A horse walks into a bar and the bartender says, "Why are you holding a long face?

p94.original: 这个简短的笑话（也可能是冷笑话）含有多个不一致的图式，包括：
p94.en: This short joke (and possibly a cold one) contains several inconsistent patterns, including:

p95.en: (1) We know that horses go to bars often;

p96.original: （2）马的长鼻子和用来比喻悲伤的“长脸”（long face）产生的混淆。
p96.en: (2) Confusion between the long nose of the horse and the long face (long face) which is used as a metaphor for grief.

p97.original: 然而，并非所有我们认为不一致的事情都是好笑的。一个人在人行道上被车撞了，这个就不好笑。一般而言，如果相互冲突的图式包含着威胁，或者如果情境使我们珍视的信念受到了嘲笑，我们就不会觉得好笑。然而，如果一个笑话唤醒的图式贬低了我们认为有威胁性的某个人，我们很可能会觉得它幽默。这也是我们认为许多种族主义、性别歧视或政治性的笑话有幽默感的原因。
p97.en: However, not all things that we consider inconsistent are funny. It's not funny that a man gets hit by a car on the sidewalk. In general, we would not find it funny if conflicting patterns contained threats or if circumstances made our cherished beliefs mocked. However, we may well find it humorous if a joke awakens someone whom we think is threatening. That is why we believe that many racist, sexist or political jokes have a sense of humor.

p99.original: 我们不仅有关于物体和事件的图式，还有关于人、角色，以及我们自己的图式。这些图式帮助我们判断在特定情境中应该对什么产生预期或者人们该如何表现。一个事件图式或脚本（script）由预期在特定环境以某种方式发生的相互关联的具体事件和行动顺序的相关知识所组成（Baldwin，1992）。我们有关于去餐厅、度假、听讲座、第一次约会的脚本。然而，当你的脚本与你周围其他人的脚本不同时，冲突就会出现。
p99.en: We have maps not only of objects and events, but also of people, of roles, and of ourselves. These diagrams help us to judge what should be expected in a given situation or how people should behave. An event diagram or script (script) consists of knowledge of the specific events and sequences of action that are expected to occur in a given environment in some way (Baldwin, 1992). We have scripts on going to restaurants, vacations, lectures, first date. However, when your scripts are different from those of the others around you, conflicts arise.

p100.en: The impact of culture on scripts

p101.original: 不同文化的脚本间存在差异。例如，住在保守的阿拉伯国家的美国女性经常反映，许多在美国被认为是理所当然的行为——如在无人陪同的情况下于公共场合行走、穿露出脸和腿的衣服或者开车——被当地人认为是可耻的不恰当行为。为了维持良好的关系，许多（美国的）女性改变了自身行为来适应当地的风俗。同样，美国人也期望来自其他国家的访客能够遵循美国的做法。例如，在美国餐厅就餐时，食客需给服务员15%～20%的小费——这远高于许多其他国家的惯例。
p101.en: There are differences between the scripts of different cultures. For example, American women living in conservative Arab countries often reflect the fact that many of the acts considered to be natural in the United States — such as walking in public without an escort, wearing clothes showing their faces and legs, or driving cars — are considered shameful and inappropriate by locals. In order to maintain good relationships, many women (in the United States) have changed their behaviour to adapt to local customs. Similarly, Americans expect visitors from other countries to follow United States practice. For example, when eating at a restaurant in the United States, the caterer is required to pay 15 to 20 per cent tips to the waiter, which is much higher than the practice in many other countries.

p102.original: 世界各地脚本的文化多样性来源于每种文化看待世界的独特图式。这些图式包含着当地文化的价值观。我们往往会感觉与那些和我们有相同脚本的人相处时更舒服，因为我们看待事情的方式相同，也知道应该期待什么（Abelson，1981；Schank & Abelson，1977）。不幸的是，我们对不熟悉脚本的不适感有时会引发分歧，如人们说“我尝试过互动，但实在太尴尬了，我不想再试了”（Brislin，1993）。在这个文化日益多元的世界，了解脚本和图式的力量能够帮助我们更加开放地接受他人的脚本，并且更有弹性地尝试弥合差异的新方法。毕竟人们常说，多样性是生活的调味品。
p102.en: The cultural diversity of scripts around the world is derived from the unique pattern of the world viewed by each culture. These maps contain values of local culture. We tend to feel more comfortable with people who share the same script as us, because we see things in the same way and know what to expect (Abelson, 1981); Shank & Abelson, 1977. Unfortunately, our discomfort with the lack of familiarity with scripts sometimes leads to disagreement, as people say, “I tried to interact, but it was too embarrassing to try again” (Brislin, 1993). In an increasingly multicultural world, the power of knowing scripts and drawings can help us to be more open to the scripts of others and to try new ways of bridging differences more flexibly. After all, it is often said that diversity is the spice of life.
